subject: Pass the local Qwen compatibility gate
description:
## What to build

Coordinate the compatibility work that must pass before production Recall MVP implementation begins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exact local synthesis stack is pinned and documented.
- [ ] The opt-in compatibility spike proves the required Effect AI and Qwen behavior.
- [ ] A human verifies the Apple-silicon setup and records the result.
- [ ] The verified compatibility record is finalized before the epic completes.

## Source

Derived from `.specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-slice-1-mvp.md`, especially Gate 0.
context:
## Execution context

Gate 0 is a hard phase gate. Production Recall implementation must not begin unless its child Tickets complete successfully.

## Relevant project context

- Source of truth: `.specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-slice-1-mvp.md`.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and the PRD before work.
- Consult `.repos/effect/LLMS.md`, `.repos/effect/.patterns/`, and Effect AI source/tests before using Effect APIs.

## Dependency context

None. This epic blocks the production Recall MVP epic.

## Verification expectations

- Child Tickets provide the concrete verification evidence.
- Run `bun run check` after repository changes.

subject: Pin and document the local Qwen stack
description:
## What to build

Select and pin the candidate local synthesis stack and create the Apple-silicon setup guide required to exercise it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the exact `llama-server` version or commit.
- [ ] Record the exact Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M URI, filename, size, and checksum.
- [ ] Pin the compatible `@effect/ai-openai-compat` dependency and lockfile entry.
- [ ] Create `docs/recall-local-synthesis-setup.md` with all ten PRD-required setup topics.
- [ ] Document a 16,384-token context window unless compatibility evidence requires another value, never below 8,192.
- [ ] Document loopback-only startup, fixed model alias, Jinja, and non-thinking settings without adding server lifecycle management.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Human setup guide,” “Pinned compatibility stack,” and “Dependency requirements.”
context:
## Execution context

Produce a precise candidate stack that the compatibility spike and human verification can exercise. Values become final only after the human gate passes.

## Relevant project context

- Primary files: `packages/core/package.json`, `bun.lock`, `docs/recall-local-synthesis-setup.md`.
- The repository pins Effect `4.0.0-beta.100`; do not upgrade Effect packages unless a proven blocker requires explicit reconsideration.
- Consult vendored third-party source before selecting APIs. Clone missing libraries under the repository’s approved read-only vendor location when required by `AGENTS.md`.
- Do not change `node-llama-cpp`, EmbeddingGemma, libSQL, or semantic-index compatibility.

## Dependency context

None within Gate 0. The compatibility spike depends on these candidate pins and instructions.

## Verification expectations

- Verify manifest and lockfile consistency.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Build the Effect AI compatibility spike
description:
## What to build

Create an opt-in compatibility spike proving Effect AI structured generation against the pinned local Qwen server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reject non-loopback URLs before any request.
- [ ] Reach the local server through Effect AI structured generation.
- [ ] Prove the server accepts the generated structured-output JSON Schema.
- [ ] Prove Qwen runs in non-thinking mode.
- [ ] Decode both `answered` and `not_found` through the intended Effect Schema.
- [ ] Map malformed output, unavailable server, and incompatible server to precise failures.
- [ ] Prove no hosted request or fallback occurs.
- [ ] Keep live-model execution opt-in and outside normal `bun run check` tests.

## Source

Derived from PRD section “Compatibility proof.”
context:
## Execution context

Build a focused compatibility proof, not an answer-quality benchmark and not the final production Recall workflow.

## Relevant project context

- Use `LanguageModel.generateObject`; do not request JSON text and parse it manually.
- Use Effect Schema for all untrusted and model-produced structures.
- Endpoint validation, provider construction, and model selection belong in adapters or Layers.
- Follow repository TypeScript rules: no `any`, assertions, non-null assertions, `import type`, or inline type-only imports.
- Consult `.repos/effect/LLMS.md`, `.repos/effect/.patterns/`, and relevant Effect AI source/tests first.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the candidate stack and setup guide because the spike must exercise those exact values.

## Verification expectations

- Run deterministic tests without a live server.
- Run `bun run check`.
- Document the exact opt-in command for the human verification Ticket.

result.summary: Added an opt-in Effect AI local-Qwen compatibility spike with typed endpoint and provider failure handling.
result.details: Implemented LanguageModel.generateObject for answered and not_found through one strict Effect Schema, fixed local model configuration with request-level non-thinking mode, deterministic fake-HTTP contract coverage, and a live Bun runner whose HTTP transport disables redirects. Restored the missing pinned Apple-silicon setup guide and documented the exact human verification command.
decisions: Kept the spike isolated from production Recall and normal live execution; bun run check exercises only deterministic fake HTTP while the human gate opts into the pinned local server.
verification: bun run --cwd packages/core test -- local-qwen-compatibility.test.ts: passed (7 tests)
bun run check: passed (all package typechecks; 10 core files/117 tests plus all workspace suites)
Opt-in guard command without AGENTIC_MEMORY_QWEN_COMPATIBILITY exited nonzero before any live request

subject: Verify the local Qwen compatibility gate
description:
## What to build

Manually verify the pinned Apple-silicon local synthesis setup and compatibility spike.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Install the exact documented `llama-server` version on supported Apple-silicon macOS.
- [ ] Download the exact Qwen artifact and verify filename, size, and checksum.
- [ ] Start the server on loopback with the fixed alias and documented settings.
- [ ] Verify `/v1/health` and `/v1/models` identify the required model.
- [ ] Run the opt-in compatibility spike and record complete pass/fail evidence.
- [ ] Stop and report the blocker if any required proof fails; do not approve a fallback adapter implicitly.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Human setup guide,” “Compatibility proof,” and the completion criterion that Gate 0 passes.
context:

subject: Deliver the Recall Slice 1 MVP
description:
## What to build

Progressively replace public Recall with a semantic-only, Markdown-authoritative, locally synthesized product that ends at the Slice 1 PRD contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Public Recall becomes runnable from the first semantic slice onward.
- [ ] No lexical, deterministic, QMD, source-inclusive, or hosted fallback remains.
- [ ] Each implementation slice leaves the command working against an existing indexed vault.
- [ ] The final flow hydrates current Markdown, prepares bounded safe evidence, synthesizes one grounded claim, abstains safely, and reports complete readiness and failures.
- [ ] Normal tests use deterministic fake external adapters and `bun run check` passes.

## Source

Derived from `.specs/PRD-agentic-memory-recall-slice-1-mvp.md` plus the approved conversation decisions to use progressive public cutover, allow temporary intermediate output, remove legacy Recall immediately, and require TDD for the initial semantic subtasks.
context:
## Execution context

This epic intentionally supersedes the PRD’s implementation-order and backward-compatibility instructions while preserving the PRD’s final product contract. Intermediate public answers may temporarily expose indexed or hydrated passages until later child Tickets harden them.

## Relevant project context

- Current Recall: `packages/core/src/recall/` and `packages/cli/src/commands/recall.ts`.
- Semantic prerequisites: `packages/core/src/semantic/EmbeddingModel.ts`, `MarkdownChunking.ts`, `SemanticIndex.ts`, and `SemanticIndexRepository.ts`.
- Status contract: `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts` and `status-output.ts`.
- Benchmark package must remain a black-box caller.
- Follow `AGENTS.md` and Effect v4 source guidance.

## Dependency context

The entire production phase is blocked by the Gate 0 epic because the PRD and approved plan require compatibility proof first.

## Verification expectations

- Child Tickets own focused verification.
- Run `bun run check` after every implementation slice.

subject: Cut recall over to semantic results
description:
## What to build

Coordinate the first public semantic-only Recall cutover, including current-index enforcement, exact semantic hit selection, the source-free contract, typed CLI failures, and removal of obsolete implementations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four child subtasks complete through their approved public test seams.
- [ ] Public Recall returns an indexed semantic result from an existing current vault index.
- [ ] Sources cannot participate in top-K or the request contract.
- [ ] Lexical, deterministic, and QMD Recall implementations and fallbacks are absent.
- [ ] Introduced operational failures have actionable CLI mappings.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Semantic retrieval,” “Ranking and eligibility policy,” “Public contract,” and “Cutover and legacy removal,” modified by the approved immediate public cutover and no-backward-compatibility decisions.
context:
## Execution context

This parent Ticket completes only when all child subtasks are done. Its first working state may return indexed chunk text temporarily; later Tickets restore Markdown authority and final output safety.

## Relevant project context

- Core seam: exported `recall` interface from `packages/core/src/recall/Recall.ts`.
- CLI seam: `packages/cli/src/commands/recall.ts`.
- Semantic search internals must remain hidden behind the semantic module’s interface.
- Source exclusion must occur before the eligible top-K budget.

## Dependency context

No child-level dependency beyond the blocked parent epic. The subtasks record their own true ordering.

## Verification expectations

- Use the child subtasks’ red-to-green cycles.
- Run `bun run check` after each completed child.

subject: Require a current index before recall
description:
## What to build

Make a current semantic index mandatory before Recall performs any retrieval or answer work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A lexically answerable vault with no index fails instead of returning a lexical answer.
- [ ] Missing, stale, and incomplete indexes fail before query embedding.
- [ ] Tests prove the embedding adapter is not accessed on these failures.
- [ ] No indexing, repair, synchronization, deletion, or model download occurs.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Singular-question scope,” “Semantic retrieval,” and “Failure semantics.”
context:
## Execution context

Use strict TDD through the exported core `recall` interface. Work one behavior at a time: write a failing public-seam test, observe the expected failure, add only enough implementation to pass, then repeat.

## Relevant project context

- Primary seam: `@urban/agentic-memory-core/recall/Recall`.
- Use temporary vaults and fake external adapters; do not test private methods or internal call graphs.
- `requireCurrentSemanticIndex(vaultPath)` is the single mandatory readiness operation.
- Follow repository TypeScript and Effect rules.

## Dependency context

None within the semantic cutover task. This behavior must exist before semantic hit selection.

## Verification expectations

- Capture red evidence for the first failing behavior.
- Run focused tests after every green cycle.
- Run `bun run check` before completion.

subject: Return the nearest semantic recall hit
description:
## What to build

Replace the lexical Recall result with the nearest eligible exact-cosine semantic hit and remove the obsolete retrieval and answer implementations once behavior is green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recall formats the question with `formatQueryEmbeddingInput` and embeds it through `EmbeddingModel`.
- [ ] libSQL exact-cosine ordering determines the selected hit.
- [ ] `sources/` is excluded before the top-10 eligible budget.
- [ ] No eligible hit returns `not_found`.
- [ ] The temporary public answer is the best indexed semantic chunk.
- [ ] Lexical scoring, ranking, pooling, deterministic assembly, QMD scaffolding, obsolete tests, and fallback wiring are deleted after semantic behavior passes.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Semantic retrieval,” “Ranking and eligibility policy,” and “Cutover and legacy removal,” plus the approved progressive cutover decision.
context:
## Execution context

Use strict red-to-green TDD through the exported core `recall` interface. Add one behavior at a time: nearest-hit selection, source exclusion before top-K, then no-eligible-hit abstention. Only after these tests are green, remove dead legacy implementation and rerun the behavior suite.

## Relevant project context

- Use meaningful fake embeddings with independently specified expected ordering.
- Use temporary indexed vaults rather than committed derivative index artifacts.
- The semantic module must own database path, vector encoding, SQL schema, and exact search details.
- Keep `node-llama-cpp` EmbeddingGemma and semantic compatibility unchanged.
- Do not mock internal collaborators or assert implementation call structure beyond proving excluded external adapters are untouched on fail-fast paths.

## Dependency context

Blocked by mandatory current-index enforcement because query embedding and search may run only after the guard succeeds.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red before each new behavior.
- Run focused core and semantic tests after each green cycle.
- Search for and remove obsolete production references after green.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Remove source inclusion from recall
description:
## What to build

Make source inclusion unrepresentable in the core request and public Recall CLI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `includeSources` is removed from the core request schema and type.
- [ ] Supplying `includeSources` to the strict request decoder fails as an excess property.
- [ ] `--include-sources` is removed from the CLI.
- [ ] The removed flag produces the CLI’s normal unknown-flag failure.
- [ ] Black-box benchmark inputs and tests use the Slice 1 source-free contract.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Public contract” and “Core request,” plus the approved no-backward-compatibility decision.
context:
## Execution context

Use TDD through two approved seams: the exported request decoder and public CLI invocation. First drive request rejection, then drive unknown-flag behavior. Do not test CLI parser internals.

## Relevant project context

- Core contract: `packages/core/src/recall/RecallContract.ts`.
- CLI: `packages/cli/src/commands/recall.ts`.
- Benchmark remains a black-box caller and must not import Recall internals.
- Source exclusion is unconditional in Slice 1.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the working semantic hit because the source-free contract is the contract for that public implementation.

## Verification expectations

- Observe each contract and CLI test fail before implementation.
- Run focused core, CLI, and benchmark tests after green.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Map semantic recall failures publicly
description:
## What to build

Map the semantic failures introduced by the first cutover to stable public CLI failures with actionable guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing, stale, and incomplete index failures direct the user to run `agentic-memory index --vault <vault>`.
- [ ] Invalid and incompatible index failures direct the user to delete and rebuild the index.
- [ ] Query embedding and semantic search failures are distinct operational failures.
- [ ] Every mapped failure exits nonzero.
- [ ] Failure output does not expose database paths, vector details, or embedding internals.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Failure semantics” and “Automated testing.”
context:
## Execution context

Use strict TDD through public CLI stdout, stderr, and exit status. Write one failing CLI behavior test, add only its minimum mapping, and repeat for each failure category.

## Relevant project context

- CLI mapping: `packages/cli/src/commands/recall.ts` and shared CLI output helpers.
- Core errors should use stable domain reasons, not provider or repository implementation details.
- Avoid exact internal messages where stable public guidance is the intended contract.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the semantic hit implementation because it introduces the error categories this subtask maps. It can proceed independently of source-contract cleanup once that hit exists.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red and green for each CLI failure category.
- Run focused CLI tests.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Hydrate hits from current Markdown
description:
## What to build

Replace indexed text with the selected chunk reproduced by ordinal from the current authoritative Markdown document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hydrate the current owning managed Markdown document for every selected hit.
- [ ] Reproduce the selected chunk with `chunkManagedMemoryDocument` and its ordinal.
- [ ] Return hydrated Markdown chunk text rather than indexed snippet text.
- [ ] Treat missing ordinals, changed provenance, and hydration failures as typed operational failures.
- [ ] Do not expose semantic database paths or schema details to Recall.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Semantic retrieval” and “Retrieval and evidence budgets,” plus the approved second progressive vertical slice.
context:
## Execution context

Develop behavior-first through the exported core `recall` interface over controlled indexed vault fixtures. Write the failing authoritative-hydration behavior first, then drive each provenance failure independently.

## Relevant project context

- Markdown remains authoritative even though the preceding temporary slice returned indexed text.
- Reuse managed-memory parsing and `chunkManagedMemoryDocument`; do not invent alternate chunking.
- Keep fixtures opaque across the core seam; package-internal corruption fixtures may construct invalid derivative state without making callers inspect it.

## Dependency context

Blocked by completion of the semantic cutover parent because it replaces the hit representation that cutover returns.

## Verification expectations

- Observe red before hydration and each failure behavior.
- Run focused core and semantic-index tests after green.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Scrub internal recall output
description:
## What to build

Filter route-only passages and scrub internal syntax and implementation details from the runnable Markdown-backed Recall response.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Discard chunks containing only routing instructions, links, or read-when guidance.
- [ ] Do not follow or expand routes.
- [ ] Public fields contain no wikilinks, document paths, Markdown routing syntax, control-plane names, evidence metadata, provider details, or model details.
- [ ] Substantive root or map prose remains eligible after scrubbing.
- [ ] If the highest-ranked passage is ineligible, continue in semantic order to the next eligible passage.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Public contract,” “Ranking and eligibility policy,” and “Grounding and public-output validation,” plus the approved scrubbing vertical slice.
context:
## Execution context

Drive each safety behavior with a failing public Recall response or encoded JSON test before implementation. Use separate adversarial fixtures for route-only prose, wikilinks, paths, control-plane names, and internal metadata.

## Relevant project context

- The test seam is the public core response and encoded success JSON, not private sanitization helpers.
- Preserve substantive prose while removing routing-only material.
- This is deterministic preprocessing; do not call Qwen or add heuristic reranking.

## Dependency context

Blocked by Markdown hydration because scrubbing applies to authoritative reproduced content.

## Verification expectations

- Observe red before each new protection.
- Run focused public contract and core Recall tests.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Bound and deduplicate recall evidence
description:
## What to build

Prepare a deterministic bounded evidence packet from semantically ordered, hydrated, safe passages while keeping public Recall runnable with an interim evidence answer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retrieve the top 10 eligible semantic chunks in exact-cosine order.
- [ ] Select at most five passages from at most five documents.
- [ ] Select at most two passages per document.
- [ ] Deduplicate overlapping and repeated passages without heuristic reranking.
- [ ] Cap the packet at approximately 4,500 tokens before prompt overhead.
- [ ] Assign deterministic internal evidence IDs and omit unnecessary absolute paths.
- [ ] Return a deterministic safe interim answer until synthesis replaces it.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Ranking and eligibility policy” and “Retrieval and evidence budgets.”
context:
## Execution context

Use behavior-first tests through core Recall with fixture expectations specified independently of implementation. Drive ordering, deduplication, per-document limits, document/passages limits, and total budget one at a time.

## Relevant project context

- Preserve libSQL ordering; do not add lexical, lifecycle, project, entity, or historical reranking.
- Sources remain excluded before top-K.
- The evidence packet is internal and must not leak identifiers or paths publicly.
- Use one owning module for evidence budgeting and selection policy.

## Dependency context

Blocked by scrubbing because only policy-eligible safe Markdown passages may enter the evidence packet.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red and green for each budget or deduplication rule.
- Run focused evidence and core integration tests.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Reject unsupported recall questions
description:
## What to build

Reject blank and clearly multipart Recall questions deterministically before any operational dependency is accessed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve blank-input rejection.
- [ ] Accept the PRD’s singular factual examples.
- [ ] Reject multiple question marks, separated requests, semicolon-joined requests, repeated interrogative clauses, and additive request markers.
- [ ] Return typed `UnsupportedMultipartQuestion` guidance to split the request.
- [ ] Prove rejection occurs before index inspection, embedding, search, or synthesis.

## Source

Derived from PRD section “Singular-question scope.”
context:
## Execution context

Use behavior-first tests through core Recall and public CLI. Add accepted and rejected examples one at a time, with fake-adapter access tracking only to prove fail-fast ordering at real external seams.

## Relevant project context

- The validator is conservative, deterministic, and model-free.
- It runs after blank validation and before index inspection.
- Document the supported heuristic shapes; do not claim perfect natural-language detection.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the semantic cutover because it refines the new public Recall workflow. It can proceed in parallel with hydration, scrubbing, and evidence preparation.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red before each validator behavior.
- Run focused core and CLI tests.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Synthesize one local structured answer
description:
## What to build

Replace the interim evidence rendering with one structured local Qwen synthesis result using the bounded evidence packet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Model synthesis output as an unambiguous `answered` or `not_found` discriminated union.
- [ ] Use `LanguageModel.generateObject` and Effect Schema decoding.
- [ ] Treat supplied evidence as untrusted data, never instructions.
- [ ] Use the fixed `agentic-memory-qwen3-4b` alias in non-thinking mode.
- [ ] Use temperature 0, maximum output 768 tokens, 60-second timeout, and no retries.
- [ ] Accept only validated loopback HTTP configuration with no implicit default or hosted fallback.
- [ ] Map unavailable, incompatible, and malformed structured output precisely.
- [ ] Move normal benchmark tests behind a fake public subject before synthesis becomes mandatory.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Structured synthesis,” “Local synthesis configuration,” and “Automated testing.”
context:
## Execution context

Use behavior-first tests through core Recall with a fake synthesis adapter, plus adapter-level tests through fake HTTP. Drive `answered`, `not_found`, generation settings, non-thinking behavior, and each provider failure independently.

## Relevant project context

- Consult the verified Gate 0 record and Effect v4 source before implementation.
- Prompt construction and provider-agnostic AI error mapping belong behind a synthesis module.
- Endpoint validation, provider construction, and model selection belong in Layers or adapters.
- Do not expose the model, provider, prompt, evidence IDs, or paths publicly.
- Normal tests must not call live embedding or synthesis providers.

## Dependency context

Blocked by bounded evidence and singular-question validation because synthesis consumes the final packet shape and must never run for unsupported input.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red before each model or adapter behavior.
- Run focused core, adapter, CLI, and benchmark tests with fakes.

subject: Enforce grounding and safe abstention
description:
## What to build

Validate structured synthesis against supplied evidence and enforce safe answered or abstained public output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every referenced evidence ID exists in the supplied packet.
- [ ] `answered` has one nonempty answer, one nonempty factual claim, and at least one supporting evidence ID.
- [ ] `not_found` carries no answer, claim, or evidence IDs and uses deterministic public wording.
- [ ] Absent, insufficient, or unresolvedly conflicting eligible evidence produces `not_found`.
- [ ] Invalid union states, malformed output, unknown IDs, and grounding violations are typed operational failures rather than abstentions.
- [ ] Excluded sources and prohibited internal details cannot reach public fields.

## Source

Derived from PRD sections “Grounding and public-output validation” and “Failure semantics.”
context:
## Execution context

Drive validation behavior through public core Recall using controlled evidence packets and fake synthesis outputs. Add one failing case at a time for unknown IDs, missing support, invalid states, conflicts, leaks, and valid grounding.

## Relevant project context

- Do not add a second model call for entailment verification.
- Keep deterministic not-found wording owned by Agentic Memory.
- Public output remains exactly `status`, `question`, `answer`, and `warnings`.
- Invalid model output must not be silently converted to `not_found`.

## Dependency context

Blocked by structured synthesis because grounding validates its decoded domain output.

## Verification expectations

- Demonstrate red and green for each validation rule.
- Run focused grounding, core, and public contract tests.
- Run `bun run check`.

subject: Complete recall readiness and failures
